findings.title: Findings converge on D3's "absent means every instance"
findings.why_it_matters: Four distinct problems from both critics land on one rule, that a telemetry route with no instance filter covers every instance of the app: anonymous mixed rows on the listener and job lists (Finding 2), retired names counted in single-instance health (Finding 6), duplicate Code tab annotations on the parent overview (Finding 7), and stale `instance_index` callers getting app-wide data with a 200 (Finding 12). D3 was ratified on a table with two rows that don't hold ("Single-instance app: same result as today" and "the parent overview's handler count becomes the app's real count"). So the question is whether this points to a problem with the rule that should be re-evaluated, rather than addressed finding by finding. That includes whether the failure modes are simply limitations to accept. Making the filter required on per-app routes (D3's option C) would remove the local fixes for Findings 6, 7 and 12 and the per-app half of Finding 2. It would not remove the name field, because `/bus/listeners` with no `app_key` mixes every instance of every app either way.
findings.recommended: B: Keep D3's rule and address the converging findings individually.
findings.chosen: B: Keep D3's rule and address the converging findings individually.
findings.choice_reason: Asked what the name-lookup objection really avoided; kept the rule once it was explained, and the case for keeping it moved to the parent page and scope.

findings.title: `ListenerSummary` and `JobSummary` lose all instance identity while D3 mixes instances
findings.why_it_matters: D1 removes `instance_index` from both models and adds nothing in its place. Neither model has an `instance_name` field, and neither summary query selects one. After D3, `/telemetry/app/{key}/listeners`, `/jobs` and `/bus/listeners?app_key=x` return every instance's rows with nothing saying which instance owns each. Sibling instances can share a listener name and topic, so the rows can be identical apart from their counts. `/bus/listeners` with no `app_key` already mixes instances; today the index at least labels them.
findings.recommended: A: Add `instance_name: str` to `ListenerSummary` and `JobSummary`, selected from `l.instance_name` and `sj.instance_name`, and record it in D1.
findings.chosen: A: Add `instance_name: str` to `ListenerSummary` and `JobSummary`, selected from `l.instance_name` and `sj.instance_name`, and record it in D1.

findings.title: The API schema bump is missing from the ledger
findings.why_it_matters: The client will send a new query parameter and route shape and require `instance_name` on `ActionResponse`, so the PR must raise `API_SCHEMA_VERSION` and set `MIN_API_SCHEMA_VERSION` to match. `tools/check_client_floor.py` fails the PR until it does. HEAD and `v0.61.0` both report 4, so the exemption for "already above the latest release" doesn't apply. The ledger's Compatibility artifacts name neither constant.
findings.chosen: Add to the Summary's "Compatibility artifacts" bullet: `API_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`wire/src/hassette_wire/health.py`) goes to 5 and `MIN_API_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`client/src/hassette_client/version.py`) follows, per `.claude/rules/client-schema-floor.md`.

findings.title: D1's "fails to parse" claim is wrong for models with defaulted fields
findings.why_it_matters: D1's table says released client 0.61 fails to parse "summaries: required fields gone". That holds for `JobSummary`, `AppInstance`, `InstanceOutcome` and `ActionResponse`. But `ListenerSummary.instance_index` defaults to `0` and `LogEntry.instance_index` defaults to `None`, so 0.61 parses those, and every row reads as instance 0 or no instance. `tools/client_compat_ignore.txt` lists only failures, so `client_compat` won't flag these and they would appear in no migration note.
findings.chosen: Correct D1's table row for option A to separate the two groups. Required, so parsing fails: `AppInstance`, `InstanceOutcome`, `ActionResponse`, `JobSummary`, and the blocking refs. Defaulted, so 0.61 parses and reports instance 0 or none: `ListenerSummary`, `LogEntry`. Add the defaulted pair to the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer's content.

findings.title: "Alongside this release" can't happen, because the add-on bump lands first and the integration goes fully down
findings.why_it_matters: D1 already accepted that 0.61 can't parse the new responses, and this doesn't reopen that. Two things are new. First, D1 says hass-hassette bumps "alongside this release", while the Summary says "after this ships". `bump-addon` runs inside the release workflow after `publish-docker`, and the integration can only pin client 0.62 once that's on PyPI, so the add-on update always reaches users first. Second, the Assumed section understates the effect. The coordinator's one data call is `get_apps()`, so `AppInstance.index` being absent fails every poll and the whole integration goes unavailable, not just instance features. The schema bump doesn't help: `check_server_version` is a floor, so 0.61 passes against schema 5 and fails at parse, and users see the generic "can't read" warning rather than the unsupported-version repair issue. The reverse order is better behaved: client 0.62 against an old add-on raises the repair issue.
findings.recommended: A: State the order in the PR's release note (publish, then bump the integration pin at once), and correct D1 and Assumed to say the integration is fully unavailable until it bumps.
findings.chosen: A: State the order in the PR's release note (publish, then bump the integration pin at once), and correct D1 and Assumed to say the integration is fully unavailable until it bumps.

findings.title: D3's "same result as today" is false for a single-instance app after a rename
findings.why_it_matters: Today a single-instance app's health filters to its current name. Under D3 it filters by `app_key` alone, and `get_app_health` counts executions of removed handlers, so a renamed instance's health totals include the old name's history. That contradicts "renaming starts a new history" (parent D11, in Assumed). The effect is narrower than the critics state. Handler and job lists exclude retired rows and don't absorb the old name, and retirement of those rows on a rename is already handled. The frontend's default window is `since-restart`, so by default only a rename applied by live reload shows old counts, and a restart clears them.
findings.recommended: A: Correct D3's "Single-instance app" row and record that app-wide totals include retired names within the query window.
findings.chosen: A: Correct D3's "Single-instance app" row and record that app-wide totals include retired names within the query window.
findings.choice_reason: A, but file an issue: it's bigger than #3100 can handle. Filed as #3751.

findings.title: D3's parent-overview claim is wrong, and the Code tab would repeat annotations
findings.why_it_matters: D3 says the parent overview's "handler count becomes the app's real count". The count badge is on the Handlers tab, which the parent overview hides, so nothing shows that count. The critic's other suggestion, that the parent stop fetching these lists, would break something: `CodeTab` receives `displayListeners` on the parent overview, and `buildAnnotationMap` pushes `handler_method` once per listener row. Under D3 a three-instance app repeats each name three times in that line's tooltip ("on_event, on_event, on_event"). Today it reads instance 0's rows, so each shows once.
findings.chosen: Correct the D3 cell to say the parent page fetches every instance's rows, whose only reader there is the Code tab, and name `buildAnnotationMap` (`frontend/src/components/app-detail/code-tab.tsx`) in the Summary's frontend bullet, to dedupe handler names per line.

findings.title: The URL correction target is unspecified once index 0 is gone
findings.why_it_matters: The Posture says an old `?instance=0` bookmark "falls into the existing URL correction", but that correction writes `instance: 0`, which has no meaning under names. The builder has to pick a target. Correcting to the first configured name would quietly land a stale link on whichever instance is first today, and a reorder would change it, which is the bug this milestone removes. The critic's concern that a reorder-only edit leaves a stale membership check doesn't apply, because a reorder doesn't change membership.
findings.recommended: A: Correct to the same page with no `instance` param.
findings.chosen: A: Correct to the same page with no `instance` param.

findings.title: D5's table misstates option A and omits `appNeedsRestart`
findings.why_it_matters: D5's "Removed instance: Ignored at once" is untrue for A. The cached `row.instances` still holds the removed instance until the refetch lands, and that same window was scored against B. `liveIndices` also feeds `appNeedsRestart`, which D5 doesn't name, so a just-added instance's needs-restart flag is left out until the refetch, as the rollup is.
findings.chosen: Change D5's row for A to "Counted until the refetch, then gone", and add `appNeedsRestart` to the decision's situation, stating that it follows the same cached `row.instances` rule.

findings.title: CLI `--json` keys are a script contract the ledger doesn't list
findings.why_it_matters: `hassette app start|stop|reload --json` prints `instance_index` and `outcomes[].instance_index`. The ledger covers the `--instance` flag but not these keys. The "server confirmed instance" warning also compares indexes and must compare names, and `fmt_instances` falls back to `inst.index`.
findings.chosen: Add to the Summary's CLI bullet: `--json` output replaces `instance_index` with `instance_name`, the confirmed-instance warning compares names, and the footer lists the key change.

findings.title: The migration assumption can be settled now, and its cost and one-way property aren't recorded
findings.why_it_matters: Assumed hedges that the `active_*` views "may select" the column and defers the check to build. It is settled: a probe applying every migration to a scratch database on SQLite 3.45.1 found no index, view or trigger naming `instance_index`, and all four drops succeeded with the views still queryable. The cost is small: dropping the column from 2,000,000 synthetic `log_records` rows (518 MB) took 3.49 s here, and slower storage such as an add-on's SD card wasn't measured. Neither the rewrite nor the one-way property is recorded, though 018 records its own. The critic's alternative of leaving the `log_records` and `blocking_events` columns in place isn't carried, because it contradicts D1's ratified drop from all four tables and #3100's acceptance criteria.
findings.chosen: Replace the Assumed hedge with the probe result, and add that `DROP COLUMN` rewrites each table at startup (measured 3.49 s for 2M log rows) and that rolling back means deleting the telemetry database, as with 018.

findings.title: Stale callers' `instance_index` is silently ignored and returns app-wide data
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: many independent third-party callers across a version skew; about three known users here. FastAPI ignores an unknown query parameter, so `?instance_index=1` from a 0.61 client or an old script answers 200 with every instance's data, which the caller reads as instance 1's. `AppHealth` and the listener and log models have no required field to trip a parse failure. In reverse, a new CLI sending `instance_name` to an older remote server gets instance 0's data, since the CLI doesn't call `check_server_version`. The posture says "loud and minimal", but this path is silent both ways.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a stale caller's `instance_index` is ignored and answers with every instance, stated in the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a stale caller's `instance_index` is ignored and answers with every instance, stated in the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

findings.title: A renamed-and-restored instance can show its old live status
findings.why_it_matters: Under D5 store entries are keyed by `(app_key, name)` and never pruned, and `instanceLiveStatus` and `instanceLiveError` prefer a store entry over fresh data. Rename an instance and rename it back in one tab session, with no new WebSocket event for that name (a disabled or `autostart=false` instance), and the row shows the status or exception from before the rename until a reconnect clears the store. Index keys have a similar hazard today within their fixed range.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a name that returns without an event can show its pre-removal status until reconnect or reload.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a name that returns without an event can show its pre-removal status until reconnect or reload.
